mainTopic: The חלה dispute and the principle of הואיל, tested through רב חסדא and רבה's argument about baking on יום טוב for a weekday
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה. רבי יהושע rules that separated חלה is not the owner's חמץ, so a woman may let it become leavened without violating בל יראה ובל ימצא. The גמרא first suggests that the dispute with רבי אליעזר is about whether טובת הנאה counts as ממון. It rejects that idea and says instead that they argue about הואיל: since the owner could ask a חכם to cancel the separation, does the חלה still count as his? The גמרא then brings a related dispute about someone who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday. רב חסדא says he gets מלקות because we do not say הואיל. רבה says he does not, because guests might come and eat the bread today. רבה challenges רב חסדא twice. First he asks about baking on יום טוב for שבת, and רב חסדא answers that this is permitted by Torah law and only rabbinically limited, with עירובי תבשילין as a reminder. Second he asks about slaughtering a dying animal, and רב חסדא answers that the fear of money loss makes the owner truly decide to eat a כזית today. The amud ends as רבה begins a third challenge from לחם הפנים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: this חלה is not the חמץ we are warned about
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rules that separated חלה (here, חלה that became טמאה on יום טוב) is not subject to בל יראה ובל ימצא. So she may separate it, leave it until evening, and not worry if it becomes חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not the leavened bread we are warned about with 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found.' Rather, she separates the חלה and leaves it until evening, and if it becomes leavened, it becomes leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of the משנה, where רבי יהושע gives his ruling. He says the separated חלה does not count as the owner's חמץ, so there is nothing to worry about if it rises.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, רבי אליעזר was worried about this dough becoming חמץ. He suggested not designating it as חלה until it is baked. רבי יהושע disagrees: once the dough is separated as חלה, it is holy property and no longer belongs to the owner. So the owner does not transgress בל יראה ובל ימצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition 'it shall not be seen' — owning חמץ that is visible on פסח
The prohibition 'it shall not be found' — having חמץ in one's possession on פסח
We are warned (by a לאו, a negative commandment)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying חמץ is allowed on פסח in general. He is saying this specific piece of חלה does not belong to the owner, so the owner's prohibitions do not apply to it.

phrases.english: This is not the leavened bread
about which we are warned
with 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found.'
phrases.notes: The חלה is considered holy property, not the owner's.

phrases.english: Rather, she separates it and leaves it until evening,
and if it becomes leavened — it becomes leavened.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא זֶה הוּא חָמֵץ שֶׁמּוּזְהָרִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the משנה's dispute (רבי אליעזר's view appears earlier in the משנה, on the previous amud).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separated חלה is not the owner's חמץ, so letting it become leavened does not violate בל יראה ובל ימצא.

steps.title: Suggestion: the dispute is about whether the right to choose a כהן is worth money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר holds טובת הנאה is ממון, so the owner still 'owns' the חלה. רבי יהושע holds it is not ממון, so the owner does not own it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they disagree about טובת הנאה. רבי אליעזר holds טובת הנאה is money; רבי יהושע holds טובת הנאה is not money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason behind the משנה's argument. It suggests the two תנאים disagree about whether the owner's right to pick which כהן gets the חלה counts as ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner can choose which כהן receives his חלה, and someone might even pay him to give it to a particular כהן. If that right (טובת הנאה) counts as ממון, the owner still has a share in the חלה. Then he would transgress if it becomes חמץ, and that explains רבי אליעזר's worry. If the right is not ממון, the חלה is not his at all, which matches רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say — introduces a suggestion that may be rejected
The benefit of discretion: the owner's right to choose which כהן gets the gift

phrases.english: GEMARA: Let us say they disagree about the benefit of discretion.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: For Rabbi Eliezer holds: the benefit of discretion is money.
phrases.notes: So the owner still has a share in the חלה and must keep it from becoming חמץ.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה אֵינָהּ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds: the benefit of discretion is not money.
phrases.notes: So the חלה is not his, and it may become חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the underlying principle behind the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: רבי אליעזר holds טובת הנאה ממון, and רבי יהושע holds טובת הנאה אינה ממון.

steps.title: Rejection: everyone agrees about the right to choose; they argue about הואיל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone holds טובת הנאה אינה ממון. The real dispute is about הואיל: since the owner could ask a חכם to cancel the separation, is the חלה still his? רבי אליעזר says yes; רבי יהושע says we don't use that reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds that טובת הנאה is not money. Here they disagree about 'since.' רבי אליעזר holds we say 'since': if he wants, he can ask to have the separation cancelled, so it is his property. רבי יהושע holds we do not say 'since.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion and offers a different explanation of the dispute. The new explanation is about a theoretical ability (הואיל), not about the right to choose a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who separated חלה can go to a חכם for שאלה (annulment) and undo the separation, which turns the dough back into regular dough. רבי אליעזר says this potential is enough to treat the dough as his property now, so he would transgress if it becomes חמץ. רבי יהושע says we look only at the actual situation: right now it is חלה and not his.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since' — treating something based on what could be done, even if it was not done
He can request annulment (from a חכם) of the separation

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is not about טובת הנאה (everyone agrees it is not ממון). It is about whether we say הואיל: does the ability to undo the חלה make it the owner's property?
steps.confusionAlert: הואיל here is a theoretical 'could.' The owner did not actually cancel the חלה. רבי אליעזר treats the mere possibility as enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of הואיל comes up all over ש״ס, and it sets up the very next case of baking on יום טוב for a weekday.

phrases.english: No, everyone holds
the benefit of discretion is not money,
and here they disagree about 'since.'
For Rabbi Eliezer holds: we say 'since,'
and if he wants, he can ask to have it annulled —
it is his property.
And Rabbi Yehoshua holds: we do not say 'since.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the טובת הנאה explanation of step 2 and replaces it with the הואיל explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proposed reason for the dispute, not the rulings of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no need to make the תנאים argue about טובת הנאה. Both can hold it is not ממון and still disagree, because they argue about הואיל instead.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר uses הואיל (the potential to annul makes the חלה his); רבי יהושע does not.

steps.title: New dispute: baking on יום טוב for a weekday
steps.stepSummary: A related dispute is brought. רב חסדא says one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday gets מלקות; רבה says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday — רב חסדא said he is flogged; רבה said he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic of הואיל just came up, the גמרא brings a new אמוראים dispute where the same idea will matter. This step sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for food needed on יום טוב itself. Baking for a weekday seems to be a forbidden מלאכה, so רב חסדא says he gets מלקות. רבה says he does not. As the גמרא will explain, רבה's reason is a הואיל: since guests might come, the bread could still be used on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated — introduces a dispute between אמוראים
On יום טוב for a weekday

phrases.english: It was stated: one who bakes on a Festival for a weekday,
Rav Ḥisda said: he is flogged,
Rabba said: he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought because it also involves the principle of הואיל discussed in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: baking on יום טוב for a weekday is punishable by מלקות. רבה: it is not.

steps.title: The reasons behind the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives מלקות because he rejects הואיל. רבה gives no מלקות because he accepts הואיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said he gets lashes: we do not say 'since guests might happen to come, the bread is fit for him today.' רבה said he does not get lashes: we do say 'since.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב חסדא and רבה disagree about baking on יום טוב for a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב is only allowed for food needed on יום טוב itself. רבה says the bread counts as 'for today,' since unexpected guests could show up and eat it. רב חסדא says we judge by what the person actually intends, so baking for a weekday is a real Torah violation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': reasoning that something counts as permitted because it could have been used in a permitted way
He receives lashes (מלקות) for a Torah violation
Guests might happen to come to him
It is fit for him (usable today)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of הואיל from Step 3 now returns in a new area of law. The rest of this passage tests whether רב חסדא can live without it.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: he is flogged.
We do not say 'since
guests may happen to come to him
the bread is fit for him (today).'
Rabba said: he is not flogged.
We do say 'since.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר לוֹקֶה: לָא אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the dispute introduced in Step 4, linking it to הואיל from Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: no הואיל, so he gets מלקות. רבה: we say הואיל, so no מלקות.

steps.title: רבה asks how one may bake on יום טוב for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב חסדא: without הואיל, how is it ever allowed to bake on יום טוב for שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to רב חסדא: According to you, who say we do not use 'since,' how can people bake on יום טוב for שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב חסדא's view using a common practice: baking on Friday יום טוב for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food baked on Friday יום טוב for שבת is not meant for יום טוב itself. With הואיל, it is easy to permit, because guests could still come and eat it today. Without הואיל, רב חסדא seems unable to explain why this is allowed.

phrases.english: Rabba said to Rav Chisda:
According to you, who said
we do not say 'since,'
how may one bake on a Festival for Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה לְרַב חִסְדָּא: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ לָא אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's position from Step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Baking on יום טוב for שבת is accepted practice. Without הואיל, it would be a Torah violation.

steps.title: The answer: עירובי תבשילין permits it
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that baking for שבת is permitted because of עירובי תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is permitted because of עירובי תבשילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends himself: the permission comes from עירובי תבשילין, not from הואיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי תבשילין is a dish a person prepares before יום טוב so that he may continue cooking on יום טוב for שבת. רב חסדא says this is the source of the permission.

keyTerms.meaning: Cooked food set aside before יום טוב, which allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: He said to him:
Because of the eiruv tavshilin.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only הואיל can explain baking on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: עירובי תבשילין is what permits it.

steps.title: Can a rabbinic עירוב permit a Torah prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: רבה objects: עירובי תבשילין is only a rabbinic device. How can it permit something the Torah forbids?
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of עירובי תבשילין, we permit a Torah prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If baking for another day is a Torah violation, as רב חסדא says, a rabbinic enactment cannot make it permitted. The rabbis lack the power to permit what the Torah forbids.

phrases.english: And because of the eiruv tavshilin
do we permit a Torah prohibition?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם עֵירוּבֵי תַּבְשִׁילִין שָׁרֵינַן אִיסּוּרָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that עירובי תבשילין permits baking for שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic enactment cannot override a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: By Torah law, שבת needs may be done on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the Torah itself allows preparing for שבת on יום טוב. The rabbis forbade it, and the עירוב is only a reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By Torah law, what is needed for שבת may be done on יום טוב. It was the rabbis who made a decree against it, in case people would say one may bake on יום טוב even for a weekday. And since the rabbis required עירובי תבשילין, there is a clear marker.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא clarifies that baking for שבת was never a Torah problem, so the עירוב is not overriding any Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת needs count as permitted on יום טוב by Torah law. The rabbis banned it only so people would not think weekday baking is also allowed. The עירוב serves as a reminder (היכירא) that lets the rabbis lift their own ban, while weekday baking stays a Torah violation.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is NOT saying the עירוב overrides the Torah. He is saying the Torah never forbade baking for שבת in the first place. The עירוב only removes a rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא צוֹרְכֵי שַׁבָּת נַעֲשִׂין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: By Torah law, Shabbat needs may be done on a Festival,
and it is the Sages who decreed against it,
a decree lest people say
one may bake on a Festival even for a weekday.
And since the Sages required an eiruv tavshilin,
he has a clear marker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא צוֹרְכֵי שַׁבָּת נַעֲשִׂין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by reframing the prohibition as rabbinic only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Baking for שבת on יום טוב is a Torah prohibition, so the עירוב would be overriding Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah allows שבת needs on יום טוב. Only a rabbinic decree forbids it, and the עירוב acts as the reminder that removes that decree.

steps.title: A new challenge from the case of a dying animal
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a ברייתא: on יום טוב, a dangerously sick animal may be slaughtered only if there is time to eat a כזית of it roasted before nightfall. He notes the wording: 'can eat,' even if he does not actually want to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: A dangerously sick animal: one may not slaughter it unless he can eat from it a כזית of roasted meat while it is still day. 'Can eat' means even though he does not actually want to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה opens a second challenge by quoting a ברייתא and pointing out its precise wording. This is setup for the attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner slaughters the dying animal to save its meat for later, before it dies and becomes forbidden. The ברייתא only requires that he COULD eat a כזית on יום טוב, not that he actually does. רבה reads this as a requirement of mere possibility, which sounds just like הואיל.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to him (from a source)
A dangerously ill animal, likely about to die
An olive-sized amount of roasted meat

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
A dangerously ill animal,
one may not slaughter it unless there is enough time
that he can eat from it
an olive-bulk roasted while it is still day.
'He can eat',

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא בָּעֵי לְמֵיכַל.
phrases.english: even though he does not want to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is answered, רבה starts a second challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows slaughter based only on the ability to eat, not actual eating, which implies הואיל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about בהמה המסוכנת on יום טוב

steps.title: Without הואיל, why may he slaughter?
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that his view explains the ברייתא easily through הואיל, but רב חסדא cannot explain why the slaughter is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for me, since I say 'since': since he could eat if he wanted, for that reason he may slaughter. But for you, who says we do not say 'since,' why may he slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה completes his attack: the ברייתא fits his view, and he demands that רב חסדא explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With הואיל, the slaughter counts as being for יום טוב, because he could eat it today. Without הואיל, the slaughter is really for after יום טוב, which should be forbidden. רב חסדא answers this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine according to me

phrases.english: Granted, according to me, who says 'since':
'since if he wants to eat, he can eat'
for that reason he may slaughter.
But according to you, who said
we do not say 'since,'
why may he slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up by the ברייתא in Step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only הואיל explains why slaughter is allowed when he does not actually intend to eat on יום טוב. Without it, the ברייתא makes no sense.

steps.title: רב חסדא's reason: the owner would lose money
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the slaughter of the dying animal is permitted because of הפסד ממונו, the owner's money loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is permitted because of his monetary loss.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רבה's challenge. He explains why the sick animal may be slaughtered without using the idea of הואיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had said that only הואיל explains the ברייתא. רב חסדא offers a different reason. If the animal dies on its own, it becomes a נבלה and the owner loses its value, so the slaughter is allowed to prevent that loss.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces a reply)
An animal that died without proper slaughter, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: He (Rav Chisda) said to him (Rabba):
Because of his monetary loss.
phrases.notes: If the animal dies by itself, it is worthless as food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's claim in Step 11 that רב חסדא cannot explain why the slaughter is permitted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reason: replaces הואיל with money loss as the basis for permitting the slaughter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without הואיל, רב חסדא has no way to permit this slaughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaughter is permitted because of the owner's money loss.

steps.title: Can money loss override a Torah prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: רבה objects in surprise: should a Torah prohibition be permitted just because someone would lose money?
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of monetary loss we permit a Torah prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב חסדא's answer. He asks how a money concern could permit something the Torah forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב חסדא's view, slaughtering when the meat is not needed for יום טוב is a Torah violation. Money loss is not a known reason to override a Torah law. So רבה says this answer cannot work.

phrases.english: And because of his monetary loss
do we permit a Torah prohibition?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. It means: surely not!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם הֶפְסֵד מָמוֹנוֹ שָׁרֵינַן אִיסּוּרָא דְאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב חסדא's answer in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that money loss permits the slaughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money loss has no power to override a Torah prohibition. So it cannot be the reason the slaughter is allowed.

steps.title: Money loss makes him truly decide to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא clarifies that money loss does not permit anything by itself. Because of the loss, the owner decides to eat a כזית. Meat cannot be eaten without שחיטה, so the slaughter is a real יום טוב need.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. Because of his monetary loss, he made up his mind to eat a כזית. And it is impossible to have a כזית of meat without slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains what he really meant. The money loss is not the permission. It is only the reason the person decides to eat some meat today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner really plans to eat a כזית on יום טוב, the slaughter becomes ordinary food preparation for יום טוב, which is permitted. The money loss only creates the desire to eat. The permission comes from the real eating, not from the money. This is why the ברייתא requires enough time to eat a כזית before nightfall.

keyTerms.meaning: He made up his mind / decided
An olive's volume, the minimum amount that counts as eating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב חסדא is saying that money loss overrides the Torah. He agrees with רבה that it cannot. The money loss only explains why the person truly wants to eat. His real intention to eat is what makes the slaughter permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה permits the slaughter because of הואיל: he could eat, even if he doesn't want to. רב חסדא permits it because the money loss makes the owner actually decide to eat a כזית, so the slaughter is a real יום טוב need.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
phrases.notes: Meaning: yes, money loss plays a role, but not the way you think.

phrases.english: because of his monetary loss —
he decided in his heart to eat an olive's volume,
and it is impossible to have an olive's volume of meat
without slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אִין: מִשּׁוּם הֶפְסֵד מָמוֹנוֹ גָּמַר בְּלִבּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's objection in Step 13 by explaining how the money loss actually works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the mechanism: money loss is an indirect cause that creates a real יום טוב eating need. It is not a direct permission.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא seemed to say that money loss directly permits a Torah prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money loss leads the owner to decide to eat a כזית. Eating requires שחיטה, so the slaughter is permitted food preparation for יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the core difference between the two views. רבה relies on what the person could do (הואיל). רב חסדא requires what the person actually intends to do.

steps.title: רבה opens a new objection from לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רבה begins another objection against רב חסדא, quoting a source about לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection to him: לחם הפנים...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבה starts quoting a new source about לחם הפנים to challenge רב חסדא again, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איתיביה tells us a formal objection from a source is coming. The topic is לחם הפנים, the bread placed on the שולחן in the בית המקדש. The details of the challenge will appear when the source continues.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a source)
The showbread, placed weekly on the Table in the Temple

phrases.english: He (Rabba) raised an objection to him: The showbread
phrases.notes: The quoted source continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב חסדא answered the sick-animal challenge, רבה turns to a new source to attack his position again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's position. The exact point under attack only becomes clear when the לחם הפנים source continues on the next amud.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. The source about לחם הפנים is about to be quoted as a new challenge.
